title: Accessibility and keyboard interaction
learningObjectives: Explain accessibility and keyboard interaction and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Accessible interactions use semantic HTML controls, meaningful labels, logical focus order, visible focus, keyboard operability, and appropriate status announcements. Native buttons, links, inputs, and form elements provide built-in behaviour that custom controls must otherwise recreate.
understand.whyItMatters: A control that works only with a pointer excludes keyboard users and may also fail for assistive technology. Use native elements first and add ARIA only when native semantics are insufficient.
understand.analogy: Keyboard accessibility is like ensuring every control has a clear route through the interface, not only a mouse path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The native button is keyboard-operable. aria-expanded communicates state, and aria-controls identifies the controlled region.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred starting point for an accessible interactive control?
questions.explanation: Native elements provide keyboard and accessibility behaviour that custom elements would need to recreate.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
